newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ seeks car production partner - paper.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ seeks car production partner - paper.

text.p: Slovakia's largest steel maker VSZ is seeking a partner to build a car plant in Slovakia aimed mainly at the domestic, Russian and Ukrainian markets, a senior VSZ official was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
"I am convinced that Slovakia will produce cars," VSZ Supervisory Board Chairman Alexander Rezes said in an interview with the independent daily Narodna Obroda.
"But (the cars) will not be produced by VSZ but by a joint-stock company which will consist of more Slovak subjects," Rezes said without elaborating.

He added that VSZ would prefer to set up the plant in Kosice, eastern Slovakia, the seat of the steel giant because of access to VSZ infrastructure and proximity to the Ukraine and Russia via a wide-gauge railway which leads into Kosice.
VSZ officials denied that they were in talks on a car production plant with Japanese carmaker Toyota Motor Corp.
"I do not know of talks with any concrete Japanese carmaker. The speculation around Toyota is a misunderstanding," VSZ President Jan Smerek said in the same interview.
But he added that unspecified financial groups had been formed both in Slovakia and Japan to discuss the project.
"We are negotiating with (Japan's) Nomura Bank....but these talks are still only very preliminary," Jan Seno, VSZ Vice-President for finance said earlier this month.
After a trip to Japan at the beginning of April, Finance Minister Sergei Kozlik said Toyota was considering locating a car produciton plant in eastern Slovakia.
Toyota has so far not commented on the project.

VSZ is already diversifying into other fields in order to offset the cyclical nature of the steel industry, and has heavily invested in the past two years in banking, insurance, services and even sports teams.
Last year, VSZ invested 2.5 billion crowns in its main steel production which, Smerek said, was enough.
Investments in 1997 are estimated at 3.5 billion crowns of which the major part will go to the production of zinc-coated sheet steel.
